conservative.read: This conservative plan aims for capital preservation with a target of ~1.5% per month. It significantly de-risks the portfolio by eliminating leveraged ETFs and reducing concentration. Expect lower volatility and drawdowns, but also more modest returns.

balanced.read: This balanced plan prioritizes risk-first growth, targeting ~2.5% per month. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad index exposure with quality tech. Expect moderate volatility and growth potential, with a focus on managing downside risk.

aggressive.read: This aggressive growth plan targets ~4% per month by leaning into leveraged ETFs and high-scoring setups. This approach significantly raises both upside potential and drawdown risk. Leveraged ETFs experience daily decay and rebalancing, meaning substantial losses can occur rapidly without strict stop discipline.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure.

income.read: This income plan aims for ~1% per month by rotating into income-focused ETFs. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable distributions over growth. While providing cash-like income, distributions are variable and NAV can still fall in a selloff, so it is not a savings account.
